customer.business: Growth Buddy, a low-effort money-and-habits coach app for India
customer.target: Salaried 22 to 30 year olds in Indian metros (Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad, Chennai, Mumbai, NCR) who feel their salary disappears and want to improve their lifestyle without maintaining trackers
customer.where: India, online (Android first, also iPhone and web)

behaviours.name: Tracks nothing
behaviours.how: Checks the bank balance and UPI history when money feels short; has never kept a budget.

behaviours.name: Spreadsheet tracker
behaviours.how: Keeps a Google Sheet or Excel of expenses, updated at month end when they remember.

behaviours.name: Tried and quit apps
behaviours.how: Has installed two or three expense or habit apps (Walnut/axio, Money Manager, a habit tracker) and stopped within weeks.

behaviours.name: Uses a free AA app already
behaviours.how: Has Fold, CRED Money, INDmoney or Jupiter linked and looks at it now and then.

behaviours.name: Privacy-wary
behaviours.how: Will not link a bank account or give SMS access to an app they do not know.

behaviours.name: Free-only
behaviours.how: Pays for Netflix or Prime at most; never pays for a utility app and looks for the free version.

behaviours.name: Self-improvement content fan
behaviours.how: Watches productivity and finance YouTube, buys books like Atomic Habits, starts new routines on Mondays.

objections: Fold, CRED and INDmoney already show my spends for free
Auto-tracking apps miss or duplicate transactions and I end up fixing them
I do not want to link my bank account to an unknown app
I have quit every tracker I tried within two weeks
One app for money, habits, health and food sounds cluttered
I would not pay for an expense tracker
Will it be around in a year, and is my data safe with a solo developer?
habits: you pay for almost everything by UPI on PhonePe or GPay
your salary lands on the 1st and is mostly gone by the 20th
you order food on Swiggy or Zomato three or four times a week
you live in a shared flat or PG and split bills on Splitwise
you keep meaning to start going to the gym
you spend an hour on WhatsApp and Instagram every evening

pitch:
Growth Buddy, a phone app (Android, iPhone and web) that keeps your money and daily habits on track with almost no typing.
Link your bank through RBI Account Aggregator and spends fill in on their own; anything it misses, you fix by typing one sentence ("spent 450 on lunch") in the app or on WhatsApp.
Every morning it shows one thing to do today, and a weekly review of where your money and habits went. Habits, water, sleep, food photos and steps are in the same app if you want them.
Free: tracking, quick add, habits and reminders. Pro: Rs 99 a month or Rs 999 a year, adds AI estimates (receipt and food photos), the Buddy AI coach chat, family sharing and deeper reports.
Made by a solo developer in India; new app, no reviews yet.
